questions.question: The midpoint theorem states that the segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is:
options: Parallel to the third side and equal to half of it
Perpendicular to the third side and equal to it
Equal to twice the third side
Equal to the third side and parallel to it

questions.question: In triangle PQR, QR = 24 cm. S is the midpoint of PQ and T is the midpoint of PR. The length of ST is:
Before you may quote the midpoint theorem, the question must give you:
options: One midpoint and a right angle
Two midpoints on the SAME side of the triangle
Midpoints on TWO DIFFERENT sides of the same triangle

questions.question: In triangle PQR with PQ = 16 cm, QR = 24 cm and PR = 20 cm, S and T are the midpoints of PQ and PR. The perimeter of triangle PST is:

subtopics.title: Proving It — Two Copies Make a Parallelogram

questions.question: The construction that starts the standard proof is:
options: Produce DE to F so that DE = EF, and join FC
Drop a perpendicular from A to BC
Draw a circle through A, B and C

questions.question: Triangles ADE and CFE are proved congruent by which condition?
options: Side-angle-side, using AE = EC, DE = EF and vertically opposite angles

questions.question: DBCF is shown to be a parallelogram because:
options: All four of its sides are equal
One pair of opposite sides, DB and FC, are both equal and parallel

questions.question: Once DBCF is a parallelogram, DF = BC. The final step to DE = ½BC uses the fact that:
options: BC was bisected by the construction
DE and BC are alternate angles
Triangle ADE has half the area
DE is half of DF, because F was constructed so that DE = EF

subtopics.title: The Converse — One Midpoint and a Parallel Line

questions.question: The converse of the midpoint theorem says that a line through the midpoint of one side, parallel to a second side:
options: Is equal to the second side
Is perpendicular to the third side

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 14 cm, AD = 7 cm with D on AB, and DE is parallel to BC with E on AC. Which conclusion is correct?
options: E is the midpoint of AC, so DE = half of BC
Nothing follows, because only one midpoint is given

questions.question: In that triangle, BC = 18 cm. The length of DE is:
The reason most memoranda expect when you use the converse is:
options: Line through midpoint parallel to second side
Alternate angles, DE parallel to BC

questions.question: In the rider on triangle ABC with midpoints D, E and F of AB, AC and BC, DEFB is proved to be a parallelogram by aiming at which condition?
options: One pair of opposite sides both equal and parallel

questions.question: In that rider, DE = BF because:
options: DE and BF are opposite sides of a rectangle
Both are equal to half of BC — DE by the midpoint theorem, BF because F is the midpoint of BC
They look the same length in the sketch

questions.question: A learner is given DE = 12 cm, where D and E are midpoints of AB and AC. They write BC = 6 cm. The error is:
options: Using the converse instead of the theorem
Halving when they should double — the join is the SHORT segment, so BC = 24 cm

questions.question: Which of these is a legitimate reason to treat a point as a midpoint in a rider?
options: It looks like the middle of the segment in the diagram
The two halves appear roughly equal when measured with a ruler
The question states it, or the diagram carries matching tick marks on the two halves

questions.question: The brace nailed between the halfway marks on two rafters is:
options: Parallel to the base beam and exactly half its length
At right angles to the base beam
The same length as the base beam

questions.question: If the base beam is 10 metres, the brace across the halfway marks measures:
Reading the roof backwards: the brace measures 3 metres. The base beam is:
In the scissors-and-spin explanation, the small top triangle is turned a half-turn about:
options: The middle of the base beam
A corner of the base beam
The halfway mark on one rafter

questions.question: After the spin, the two pieces together form a parallelogram. The 'half' comes from the fact that:
options: Two brace-lengths lie along the top, and the top of a parallelogram equals its bottom — the base beam
A parallelogram has four equal sides
The brace was measured with a ruler

questions.question: The 'parallel' half of the theorem falls out of the same picture because:
options: The top and bottom of a parallelogram always run parallel
The brace was nailed level by the builder

questions.question: Joining all THREE middle marks of a triangle produces:
options: Four identical small triangles, each with sides half as long as the original's

questions.question: The theorem's 'calling card' in an exam question is:
options: A right angle in the triangle
A circle drawn through the vertices
The word 'midpoint', or matching tick marks, on TWO different sides of one triangle

questions.question: When you quote the midpoint theorem, the advice is to write down:
options: Both conclusions — the parallel AND the half — even if the question seems to want only one
The construction used in the proof

questions.question: A question gives you ONE midpoint and tells you the line from it is parallel to another side. This is:
options: Enough — that line lands exactly on the middle of the remaining side
Only useful if the triangle is isosceles
A reason to use congruent triangles instead

questions.question: Which reason belongs beside a statement that used two given midpoints?
options: Line through midpoint parallel to second side
